AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND/AIMS
AbstractText.content: To delineate the relationship of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), obesity, and hyperandrogenism (HA) with glucose and insulin dynamics in adolescents across a broad body mass index (BMI).

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Seventy-four PCOS subjects (aged 16 years) and 82 controls (aged 16 years) were evaluated by an oral glucose tolerance test. Subjects were categorized by BMI: normal weight (21 ± 0.4), overweight/obesity (OO; 33 ± 1.0), and severe obesity (SO; 48 ± 1.4). Indices of glucose and insulin dynamics were determined. Multiple linear regression analysis was used to evaluate the contribution of PCOS, HA, and BMI to these indices.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: BMI was significantly associated with systolic and diastolic blood pressure and insulin resistance. A significant interaction between BMI and PCOS and indices of post-glucose load was observed. The mean difference in peak glucose, early glucose response, area under the curve for glucose, and glucose effectiveness (SgIo) between PCOS and control subjects was significantly different between OO and SO. In PCOS subjects, testosterone was positively associated with BMI, fasting insulin, early insulin response, and diastolic blood pressure, and negatively associated with SgIo.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Abnormal glucose dynamics in adolescents with PCOS is mainly due to SO. The combination of PCOS and SO has a synergistic effect on glucose dynamics when compared to all other groups.
